analysis: The code calls substring(a, b) after computing a and b. The documentation states IndexOutOfBoundsException if beginIndex is negative, endIndex > length, or beginIndex > endIndex. In the code, a = Math.max(r.length() - length + 1, 0) ensures a >= 0, so beginIndex is never negative. b = Math.max(a, r.length()) ensures b >= a, so beginIndex > endIndex cannot occur. However, b can exceed r.length() when a > r.length(), which happens if length <= 0 (since a = r.length() - length + 1 > r.length() when -length + 1 > 0, i.e., length < 1). In that case, endIndex > r.length() triggers IndexOutOfBoundsException. The preceding check (r.length() > length) does not prevent this scenario. Thus the exception is only partially avoided.
answer: IndexOutOfBoundsException is not fully avoided because the condition endIndex > string length can occur when the parameter length is less than or equal to 0.
remark: The exception triggers when length <= 0 because then a = r.length() - length + 1 > r.length(), so b = a (since a > r.length()), and substring(a, b) has endIndex b > r.length(), causing IndexOutOfBoundsException. For positive length, b equals r.length() and the call is safe.
